bibliography.abstract: Traffic flow prediction is a core supporting technology for intelligent transportation systems. It uses historical data to infer future traffic dynamics in specific areas, thereby helping to alleviate congestion and improve resource allocation efficiency. Traditional neural networks struggle to break through accuracy limits due to their reliance on singular feature modeling, while large language models (LLMs) suffer from insufficient capture of spatial topological information and mining spatiotemporal correlation. This study proposes a Dynamic Fusion Large Language Model (DF-LLM) for traffic flow prediction. The model incorporates three core components: spatiotemporal embedding module, spatiotemporal fusion module, and LLM backbone. The spatiotemporal embedding module enables synergistic representation of multi-scale spatiotemporal features. The spatiotemporal fusion module integrates spatial topology and dynamic dependencies via graph convolution. The LLM backbone adopts a differentiated parameter adaptation strategy to balance training efficiency and traffic data adaptability. Additionally, it introduces a context aggregation attention module to strengthens global dependencies. More importantly, the LLM backbone takes the residual connections to mitigate the gradient vanishing in deep networks. Experiments show that DF-LLM has achieved better performance by comparing the metrics on all the four datasets.
bibliography.title: A Dynamic Fusion Large Language Model for Traffic Flow Prediction

en.what: The Dynamic Fusion Large Language Model (DF-LLM) was developed to improve traffic flow prediction by combining a spatiotemporal embedding module, a graph convolution-based fusion module, and an adapted LLM backbone. The model uses a differentiated parameter adaptation strategy, a context aggregation attention module, and residual connections to capture multi-scale spatiotemporal features and global dependencies. Evaluation across four benchmark datasets demonstrated that this architecture outperforms existing traffic prediction models.
en.why: It bridges the gap between traditional neural networks that rely on singular feature modeling and large language models that typically fail to capture spatial topology and dynamic spatiotemporal correlations.
